jobs.description:
Staff Research Associate 1 (9613C), Environmental Science, Policy, and Management \#87591 About Berkeley
  
  

At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation \- driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full\-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  

Departmental Overview
  
  

The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is a multidisciplinary program that recognizes the urgency of the challenges, and the enormous opportunities that may lead to transformative change. We have award\-winning faculty in climate science, biodiversity, environmental policy, land use, and community outreach \- all driven by a collective interest in our environmental future. We strive to serve as the campus portal to environmental research and issues. Berkeley is founded on the principle of knowledge for the public good. Our department builds on this promise. We offer a portfolio of exciting undergraduate majors that offer diverse career options to students interested in biology, environmental science, environmental policy, and preparation for the health professions. Our highly ranked graduate program consistently serves as a gateway to exciting careers in research, teaching, and public outreach.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

The Staff Research Associate 1 conducts research on the colonization of grapevines by a vector\-borne plant pathogen. This position supports all aspects of a research project aimed at initiating and gathering data on a grapevine disease management strategy in California. Responsibilities include sample collection in field plots, maintenance of plants in a greenhouse facility, and molecular\-based detection of pathogens in the laboratory.
  
  

Application Review Date
  
  

The First Review Date for this job is August 5, 2026\. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  

Responsibilities
  
  

PCR\-based pathogen detection in the laboratory \- 30%
  
  

PCR\-based pathogen detection in the laboratory.
  
Total plant DNA extraction following standard protocols, followed by PCR\-based DNA amplification using quantitative PCR as a detection tool.
  
Data evaluation, entry and organization are included in this responsibility.
  
Maintenance of plants in a greenhouse facility \- 20%
  
  

Potting and pruning of plants, growing plant species for experimental manipulations; monitoring for plant health.
  
Support to general research activities in the laboratory \- 25%
  
  

Assisting with lab cleaning and organizing, assisting in other projects focused on pathogen detection, support with data organization and sample processing as necessary.
  
Experimental manipulations with plants and pathogens \- 20%
  
  

Establishing infections and monitoring plants at different time points and conditions using appropriate tools, keeping record plant disease symptoms.
  
Sample collection from field sites \- 5%
  
  

The field sites are at isolated locations.
  
Infected plant tissue will be collected from plots in California, total DNA will be extracted from these plants and pathogen genotyped using standard molecular protocols already established.
  
Required Qualifications
  
  

Experience processing and preparing grapevine samples from vineyards and greenhouse for pathogen detection. It includes DNA extraction, qPCR, and genotyping. Prior experience with grapevine diseases is highly desirable.
  
Experience maintaining grapevines in a greenhouse facility.
  
Experience organizing experimental data.
  
Preferred Qualifications
  
  

Experience infecting plants for experimental purposes on disease development.
  
Ability to reliably travel to and from the primary work location and other designated sites as required to fulfill job responsibilities.
  
Education / Training
  
  

BA or BS in Disease Ecology or Plant Pathology, or a related field, and/or equivalent experience/training. (Preferred)
  
Licenses / Certifications
  
  

Driver's License. (Required)
  
Salary \& Benefits
  
  

For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation \& Benefits website.
  
  

Under California law, the University of California, Berkeley is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. About The Position

The Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District currently has an opportunity for a dynamic and creative Environmental Analyst (Administrative Services Analyst II) for the Regulatory Division in Riverside! The Environmental Analyst would not only support and interact with District staff but would also coordinate with other public agencies and stakeholders such as developers, planning and engineering consultants, members of the public, the Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, USFWS, and other federal, state and local government agencies, and non-profit organizations.

The Regulatory Division is primarily responsible for ensuring that the District complies with state and federal environmental laws and provides support for all types of District actions such as constructing new flood control facilities, maintaining existing facilities, developing master drainage plans, and issuing encroachment permits to developers or other public agencies for their projects. The Environmental Analyst will assist with the implementation of requirements and compliance strategies through a wide variety of administrative support services such as conducting complex research, tracking pending legislation, assessing operational processes and programs and making recommendations for the development, implementation, and improvement of District operations, services and programs, coordinating with internal and external teams, and performing other related duties as required.

Candidates must have strong writing skills, excellent organization skills, and experience creating databases.

The most competitive candidates will have experience and knowledge with:

Microsoft Excel
Managing complex project lifecycles, including tracking milestones, schedules, and budgets using Microsoft Project, Microsoft Excel, or similar programs
Contract administration management, permit compliance, project coordination, and/or legal or technical research
A public works agency, natural resource agency, land use planning organization, private environmental or engineering firms

Meet the Team!

The Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District manages storm waters for conservation. and for the protection of watercourses, watersheds, public highways, life and property from flood damage. The Flood Control District is a Special District funded by property taxes. The District is not funded by, or dependent on, the County General Fund.

Examples Of Essential Duties

The Environmental Analyst will support the Regulatory Division Chief, supervisors and staff with various tasks, projects and operational needs. Examples of essential duties may include but are not limited to the following:

Manage and maintain various internal databases and create and/or update to improve existing processes.
Manage internal work orders for the Regulatory Division; track work orders and assign out using an internal digital database.

Research and analyze state and federal policies and proposed legislation that may affect District operations.
Prepare the Regulatory Division’s annual budget projections related to capital improvement projects, permit fees, compensatory mitigation costs, etc.
Review and gather reports and other documentation for submittals to various government agencies.
Manage Consultant task orders and invoices for adherence to budget and contract terms.
Track and manage the District’s Assembly Bill 52 (AB52) tribal consultation administrative records; prepare and send notices to tribes, support the District as needed with AB52 compliance.
Support the Regulatory Division Chief, supervisors and staff with meeting coordination, preparation, and implementation.
Coordinate and schedule field surveys for staff and secure access rights from various property owners as needed.
Special projects as assigned.
Conduct site visits and site analyses, including walking project sites with Environmental Specialists to provide support during project evaluations and surveys.

jobs.description:
**This position is on-site on Edwards AFB in Edwards, CA**

JT4, LLC provides engineering and technical support to multiple western test ranges for the U.S. Air Force, Space Force, and Navy under the Joint Range Technical Services Contract, better known as J-Tech II. JT4 develops and maintains realistic, integrated test and training environments and prepares our nation's war-fighting aircraft, weapons systems, and aircrews for today's missions and tomorrow's global challenges.

Working under the direction of the ES&H supervisor, an ES&H Specialist I performs general environmental and/or safety support services, investigations, analyses, and other-directed assignments as either a member of a team or as an investigator.
Employee will be responsible for the following functions/duties:
Assess and mitigate workplace hazards, perform study and analysis, and workplace inspections
Conduct mishap and incident investigations and generate reports
Interpret applicable regulations and ensure compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Air Force directives, and local safety policies and procedures
Apply confined spaces, lockout/tagout, hazardous waste requirements, and industrialized operation procedures
Identify and evaluate environmental or safety hazards and make recommendations for corrective actions
Participate in informal reviews, inspections, and audits using established procedures
Assist in the maintenance and inventory of equipment and systems
Analyze data gathered from literature or collected from investigations
Maintain familiarity with the statutory requirements related to the environmental, safety, and/or health regulations
Perform other job-related duties, as required

RANGE POSITION DESCRIPTION

Working in support of the 412 Maintenance Group (MXG), provide Unit Environmental Coordinator duties to include but not limited to:
Conduct compliance site inspections at several MXG shops throughout Edwards AFB. These compliance sites include:
Hazardous waste initial accumulation points and accumulation sites.
Hazardous Material Pharmacies and storage locations.
Air Permitted equipment and locations.
Petroleum product storage tanks.
One Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA) site.
Liaison between the 412 MXG and Edwards AFB Environmental Management regarding all environmental issues.
Conduct environmental briefings to MXG personnel to include the twice monthly New Hires brief.
Support 412 MXG and environmental management during all regulatory visits and inspections.
Support permit required sampling (annual carbon sampling and air flow study).
Implement and oversee annual subcontract to inspect, maintain and repair over 30 HAZMAT and HAZWASTE storage fire suppression systems.
Prepare monthly report that details hazardous waste generated, organizations that generated the waste, and the amount that each organization is to be billed.
Provide other duties as required/assigned.

REQUIREMENTS - EDUCATION, TECHNICAL, AND WORK EXPERIENCE

A bachelor's degree in an ES&H-related field (i.e., engineering, chemistry, biology, or other science) is preferred, or an in-depth, working knowledge of the technical concepts, principles, and requirements associated with the work unit is required for this position. This knowledge and these skills may be obtained by graduation from a two- to four-year technical institute or college or from equivalent formal technical training or military equivalent and three (3) or more years of experience in a directly related technical working environment.
In addition, an ES&H Specialist I must possess the following qualifications:
Working knowledge of word-processing and integrated software applications
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Planning/organizational skills
Ability to work under deadlines
Ability to perform detail-oriented work
The candidate must possess a valid, state issued driver's license
Must be able to obtain and maintain security clearance
Must be a U.S. citizen

SALARY

The expected salary range for this position is $78,500 to $109,500 annually.

The salary range offered for this position is a good faith description of the expected salary range this role will pay. jobs.description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

Position Overview

As an Associate, Cultural Resources and Tribal Relations, you will assist Invenergy’s cultural resources management and Tribal relations program in support of projects throughout all stages including development, pre-construction planning, construction implementation, and operations. This position serves as a subject matter expert to project teams, as well as external parties, and assists on consultant engagement strategy for cultural resources and Tribal relations-related work to support the responsible development, construction and operation of utility-scale wind, solar, geothermal and thermal energy facilities, and transmission infrastructure, across the US.

This role will coordinate and support multiple internal teams including Development, Engineering, Environmental Compliance & Strategy, Project Management, and Communications. The successful candidate will advise on the application of state and federal historic preservation laws, regulations, and policies, and will be required to ensure coordination with external cultural resources consultants, Tribal Nations, and regulatory agencies on successful compliance and implementation of cultural resources management practices.

Responsibilities

Respond to internal requests to review technical reports including cultural resources desktop studies, pedestrian inventory and testing reports, monitoring reports, ethnographies, cultural landscape studies; interpret technical jargon and details into layman’s language so project teams can understand how to manage potential risks or make decisions on next steps.
Assist in developing requests for proposals for cultural resources and Tribal engagement support services, reviewing proposals, and oversee the consultant’s work to ensure it meets company expectations and the project’s goals.
Work to ensure that the cultural resources management firms and associated work product meet internal expectations and project goals. Advise on appropriate survey scope for the specifics of a project and provide feedback on proposals regarding scope, schedule, and budget.
Support the implementation of Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, when necessary, by engaging with Tribal, state, and federal historic preservation agencies/departments on regulations and permitting requirements.
Respond to internal inquiries about when a project triggers a need for engagement with Tribal Nations, relating to federal, state, and county Tribal engagement requirements.
Manage consultant administrative items, which include purchase orders, change orders, service orders, invoice review, and budget tracking.
Identify and support the need, timing, development, and implementation for cultural and Tribal monitoring and unanticipated discovery planning while overseeing consultant efforts.
Work with internal teams to ensure confidentiality and avoidance measures of cultural resources through environmental management practices incorporating and aligning protection measures through spatial data and project specification documents.
Maintain and update record keeping systems to document, track cultural resource practices and Tribal engagement, as well as laws, regulations, policies, and requirements at the federal, state, and county level. Utilize information to support project permitting, populate permit matrices, review reports, strategic planning, and decision-making.
Maintain and regularly review internal cultural resources and Tribal information data standards and record keeping and data security protocols to ensure data are handled appropriately.

Minimum Qualifications

Demonstrated 5+ years cultural resources management experience.
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality of sensitive materials, activities, and initiatives.
Excellent technical writing and communication skills assuring documents and communications are concise and accurate.
Experience preparing and reviewing technical deliverables including desktop and field survey reports for archaeological and historic above ground cultural reviews.
Demonstrated experience developing proposals and building cost estimates for cultural resources services, requests for proposals.
Ability to navigate ArcGIS to interpret cultural resources spatial data and identify potential project risks.
Knowledge of federal and state laws, regulations, and policies pertaining to cultural resources.
Comfort and experience working in a developing program area.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to identify and solve problems.
Must be self-directed and detail-oriented, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Able to act and adapt to a fast-paced business environment with competing deadlines and quickly learn and implement internal processes.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years in the energy industry.
Advanced degree in anthropology, archaeology, or related discipline.
Experience conducting cultural resources inventories in the US including systematic pedestrian surveys with subsurface testing, and cultural resources monitoring.
Understanding of the Cultural Resource Management Industry nationwide.
Experience working with Tribal Nations on cultural resources and knowledge of Tribal sovereignty and Tribal treaty rights.

Base Pay

$98,000.00 - $118,000.00 USD Annual

Bonus: 20% - 30%

The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills.

In addition to base pay, the total annual compensation package may also include eligibility to participate in our bonus program(s) which are designed to reward individual and company performance. Your recruiter can share more about bonus eligibility for this position during the hiring process.

Invenergy offers a variety of other benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k, paid time off, etc.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Environmental Specialist is responsible for managing and executing multi-media environmental compliance programs
in a regulated aerospace manufacturing environment. This role requires hands-on ownership of air quality, hazardous waste, stormwater, and wastewater programs
in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations, with a strong emphasis on California-specific requirements
.

This position serves as the primary environmental subject matter expert
for the facility, ensuring compliance with agencies such as SCAQMD, DTSC, CUPA, LACSD and California Water Boards
. The Environmental Specialist will lead regulatory reporting, inspections, and audits, while partnering with operations, engineering, and leadership to maintain full environmental compliance and minimize risk.

Key Responsibilities

Regulatory Compliance & Environmental Programs

Manage environmental compliance programs across air, hazardous waste, stormwater, and wastewater
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations (EPA, DTSC, SCAQMD, CUPA, LACSD, and Water Boards)
Interpret environmental permits and ensure adherence to permit conditions and regulatory requirements

Air Quality Compliance (SCAQMD)

Manage facility air permits and ensure compliance with permit conditions
Track emissions (VOC/HAP) and prepare annual emissions inventories/reporting (AER)
Evaluate process changes for regulatory applicability and compliance

Hazardous Waste Management (DTSC – Title 22)

Oversee hazardous waste programs including:
Coordinate hazardous waste disposal vendors and ensure regulatory compliance

CUPA / CERS Reporting

Manage Hazardous Materials Business Plans (HMBP) and chemical inventory reporting
Maintain compliance within the California Environmental Reporting System (CERS)
Aboveground storage tank (SPCC/APSA) requirements

Stormwater Compliance (IGP / SMARTS)

Develop and maintain the Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP)
Conduct stormwater inspections, sampling, and reporting
Ensure compliance with the California Industrial General Permit (IGP) via SMARTS

Industrial Wastewater Compliance (LA County Sanitation District – LACSD)

Support industrial wastewater permit compliance, including:

Audits, Inspections & Reporting

Conduct internal environmental audits and facility inspections
Lead and support regulatory inspections (AQMD, DTSC, CUPA, LACSD, and Water Boards)
Prepare and submit regulatory reports and maintain compliance documentation

Incident Management & Continuous Improvement

Investigate environmental incidents and compliance deviations
Perform root cause analysis and implement corrective/preventive actions (CAPA)
Identify opportunities for waste reduction, emissions reduction, and environmental performance improvement

Training & Cross-Functional Support

Develop and deliver environmental compliance training to site personnel
Partner with operations, maintenance, and engineering to support compliance initiatives
Serve as environmental SME for projects, process changes, and new equipment

Required Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or related field

Experience

3–7+ years of environmental compliance experience in manufacturing, aerospace, or industrial environments
Demonstrated experience managing multi-media environmental programs (air, waste, water)
Direct experience with California environmental regulations, including:

Technical Expertise

Experience preparing and submitting environmental reports:
Knowledge of:
Ability to interpret regulatory requirements, permits, and compliance obligations

Operational Skills

Experience supporting or leading environmental audits and regulatory inspections
Strong documentation, organization, and data tracking skills
Proficiency with Excel and environmental reporting systems

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in aerospace, coatings, metal finishing, or chemical manufacturing environments
Familiarity with:
Experience with:
Professional certifications (preferred but not required):

What Success Looks Like In This Role

Ability to independently manage environmental compliance programs with minimal oversight
Confidence interacting directly with regulatory agencies and leading inspections
Strong understanding of California environmental regulations and reporting systems
Proactive identification and mitigation of compliance risks
Effective partnership with operations to maintain compliance without disrupting production

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment.

Job attendance, commitment to safety and quality, collaborative working and respect in the workplace are some of the job duties which may be impacted by a criminal history.

For informational purposes only, the range of pay for this role is $87,500 to $105,000 US Dollar (USD) Salaried based on a variety of factors. For informational purposes only, this role is eligible to participate in the Company’s Quarterly Cash Bonus Plan, paid out at the quarterly bonus factor of 2X the Company’s bonus multiple, based on the Company’s performance in the applicable quarter. Employees will receive 120 hours paid time off every year. Employees will also receive 10 paid holidays. Employees (and their families) are eligible to participate in the company's medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s 401(k) plan.

In this role, you’ll support environmental and stormwater compliance projects, including assisting clients in complying with stormwater regulations and preventing pollutants from leaving the project boundary and entering our waterways. Responsibilities will include conducting stormwater inspections, developing and implementing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and/or site stabilization plans, conducting stormwater sampling, conducting desktop evaluations, providing on-site training to construction crews, and preparing related documentation and reporting.

Depending on qualifications and experience, this position generally performs work under the supervision/guidance of more senior staff supporting both routine and complex projects. This position may support assigned initiatives and special projects. Travel and overnight travel will be required, with periodic weekend and overtime work.

Cross-training in natural resources, including wetlands and/or environmental permitting
Knowledge of water quality or Stormwater management information, techniques, practices, laws, and regulations of the job or occupational field
Knowledge of the California State Water Board Permits
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation

What You'll Bring:

BS or BA degree, preferably in an environmental discipline, sciences, or engineering
Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience supporting experience in SWPPP, including sampling and analysis, non-storm water and storm water visual observations, and preparation of Rain Event Action Plans, environmental restoration, landscape construction, and erosion control

jobs.location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, US
jobs.description:
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is seeking a motivated **Student Assistant, Environmental Compliance** to join the **Environmental Services Group (ESG)** within the **Environment, Waste \& Radiation Protection Division**. This is an exciting opportunity to gain real\-world experience supporting environmental compliance and monitoring programs at a world\-renowned national laboratory.

  



As a Student Assistant, you'll work alongside environmental professionals on meaningful projects that help protect people and the environment. You'll gain hands\-on experience conducting compliance assessments and inspections, participating in environmental sampling and monitoring, collecting and analyzing data, preparing reports and procedures, and supporting a variety of environmental programs.

  



Whether you're exploring a career in environmental science, environmental engineering, sustainability, or Environment, Health \& Safety (EHS), this position provides valuable experience, professional mentorship, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while building your resume.

  



**You will:**


* Assist in data collection and provide support for environmental compliance programs, including but not limited to, air quality, hazardous materials management, sanitary sewer, and surface water quality.
* Assist in preparing regulatory reports including analyzing and summarizing data, writing, editing and QA/QC.
* Assist with inspections and compliance assessments: collect and maintain inspection records, enter inspection data into various software systems, submit maintenance requests and complete basic stormwater and hazardous material storage inspections.
* Prepare and maintain spreadsheets to track compliance data.
* Assist with collection of environmental samples under direct supervision of EH\&S specialists or technicians.
* Consolidate, review and edit internal documents including procedures and work instructions.
* Perform data entry, spreadsheet manipulation and preparing presentation materials.

  

**We are looking for:**


* A full time student in at least their Junior year working toward an undergraduate or graduate degree in Environmental Science, Health or Engineering or similar technical degree.
* Familiarity with environmental laws and regulations and technical aspects of environmental science.
* Ability to demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to enter and manage data in various software systems and prepare graphical presentations.

  

**Additional information:**


* **Application date:** Priority consideration will be given to candidates who apply by **August 5, 2026**. Applications will be accepted until the job posting is removed.
* **Appointment type:** This is a variable 1 year, student assistant appointment with the possibility of renewal based upon satisfactory job performance, continuing availability of funds and ongoing operational needs. The incumbent will work approximately 12 hours per week during the school year and up to 20 hours per week during the summer.
* **Salary range:** The hourly range for this position is $21\.40 \- $50\.20\. Pay will be dependent on the current level of education.
* **Background check:** This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
* **Work modality:** Work will be primarily performed at:Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA with occasional telework for data\-entry projects. A REAL ID or other acceptable form of identification is required to access Berkeley Lab sites (for more information ).
* **Work authorization:** Candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

  

**Want to learn more about working at Berkeley Lab? Please visit:** **careers.lbl.gov**

  



Equal Employment Opportunity Employer: The foundation of Berkeley Lab is our Stewardship Values: Team Science, Service, Trust, Innovation, and Respect; and we strive to build community with these shared values and commitments. Berkeley Lab is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We heartily welcome applications from all who could contribute to the Lab's mission of leading scientific discovery, excellence, and professionalism. In support of our rich global community, all qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, protected veteran status, or other protected categories under State and Federal law.

jobs.title: Construction Inspector - Water Resources
jobs.description:
BKF is hiring a Construction Inspector
to execute onsite construction inspections to ensure the project is being constructed in compliance with the contract requirements and applicable permits.

Responsibilities:

General

Inspect a variety of construction including but not limited to repair of pipelines, water mains, sewers, lift stations, and treatment plants
Advises Resident Engineer or Agency Project Manager and informs contractors of any variances from approved plans and specifications
Takes samples of materials, prepares test specimens, and assist in conducting field tests, or refers samples for laboratory analysis
Checks the location of public utilities to avoid interference with construction work
Assists PM in review of project submittals, RFI's, and CCO's
Verifies acceptability of material incorporated into the project by Certificates of Compliance, shop drawings, and test reports
Maintains material and inspection records
Maintains a daily diary, photo log, contract item quantities
Other duties as assigned

Water and Wastewater infrastructure

Verify the installation and proper sealing of water pipelines, ensuring no leaks or contamination
Oversee the construction and retrofitting of stormwater, water, and wastewater treatment facilities
Ensure proper grading, drainage, and erosion control measures are in place to manage water flow and prevent pollution
Check for compliance with health and safety standards, especially related to water quality, drinking water safety, and wastewater discharge regulations
Monitor backflow prevention, cross-connection controls, and ensure plumbing systems meet sanitary standards
Test water pressure and flow in pipelines, and inspect valves, pumps, and treatment plant equipment
Oversee sewer line cleaning, pipe relining, and trenchless repair methods
Ensure that environmental impacts, such as erosion, sedimentation, and stormwater runoff, are mitigated

Environmental and Health Compliance

Inspect for compliance with the Clean Water Act, Safe Drinking Water Act, and other environmental regulations
Ensure proper handling, disposal, and treatment of wastewater to avoid pollution
Check stormwater systems to ensure they meet environmental protection requirements, including those related to wetlands and floodplains

Requirements

Minimum Education, Licensure, or Certification Required

College degree or min. 5 years' work experience in related field
Valid California Class C driver's license and an acceptable driver's record are required

Desired Certifications

Certified Public Infrastructure Inspector (CPII)
ICC Reinforced Concrete Inspection Certification
ICC Masonry Inspection Certification
ICC Welding Inspection Certification
ACI Concrete Field-Testing Technician - Grade 1 Certification
Qualified SWPPP Certification
Fall protection Safety Training
First Aid & CPR

Minimum Experience Required

2 + years of experience in the supervision or inspection of engineering construction work including reading and interpreting complex construction plans and specifications, OR
5 years' work experience in related trade/field

Desired Construction management Experience

We are seeking candidates with experience in some of the following areas. While not every item is required, experience in a combination of these areas will be highly valued:

Large diameter sewer and water pipeline, including trenchless installations
Water and wastewater treatment plants, including membrane filtration technology
Sewer lift stations
Booster pump stations
Groundwater wells
Stormwater diversion, capture, and treatment
Flood control infrastructure
SCADA installation, integration, and startup commissioning

Other Required Skills

Knowledgeable with construction methods and procedures, Caltrans and Greenbook standard plans and specifications
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Able to work well with other people, contractors, agency personnel, the public
Interacts well with other staff, public, government agencies
Able to effectively operate a computer and basic computer programs such as Word & Excel

The typical base salary range for this position is $120,640.00 - $156,000.00 annually, depending upon skills, experience, education, and geographical location, hourly wage
Competitive salaries, end of year bonuses, profit sharing, and 401k

Department of Fish and Wildlife

### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Fisheries Branch is seeking motivated candidates for a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) position. This position serves as the subject matter expert and coordinator for efforts to incorporate Parentage\-Based Tagging (PBT) into existing or new salmonid monitoring programs and anadromous hatchery practices for the purposes of conservation, mitigation and enhancement of California’s salmon fisheries. The incumbent will provide coordination and expertise for developing, implementing and integrating PBT into anadromous hatchery practices, coordinating tissue sampling in recreational and commercial fisheries, escapement, and emigration monitoring surveys. Coordinate with internal programs, and state and federal partners, ensuring that monitoring activities are scientifically sound and aligned with management needs.  

  

  

The position will provide technical expertise to interagency workgroups, participate in evaluating hatchery release strategies and interpret and communicate genetic analyses for application in fisheries and hatchery management. The position oversees the development and management of long term genetic databases, working closely with IT staff and genetic laboratories to establish data sharing agreements and integrate data systems. Responsibilities include conducting data analyses, ensuring data quality, and preparing presentations, technical reports, and annual summaries. The incumbent may also contribute to peer reviewed publications.  

  

  

Candidates should demonstrate strong initiative, professionalism, and the ability to manage complex projects independently. Effective decision making skills, adaptability, and the ability to work productively with interdisciplinary teams and diverse stakeholders are essential. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are required, including the ability to convey technical information clearly and professionally.

jobs.description:
Job Posting: SCE Supervisor



Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-525662* 

SCE Supervisor
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/4/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you ready to take on a challenge and lead a dynamic team working on high\-profile environmental projects? The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) is seeking a Limited Term Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) to oversee the Southern California Edison (SCE) workload in our Habitat Conservation Planning Program. If you are a self\-motivated individual who thrives in fast\-paced, complex work environments and is passionate about conservation and environmental protection, we want to hear from you!  

  

  

About the Role: This is a working supervisor position where you will supervise and conduct environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning functions for SCE projects. You will play a key role in ensuring compliance with the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and Lake and Streambed Alteration (LSA) agreements, working to maintain a balance between environmental protection and project progress.  

  

  

CDFW may be serving as the Lead or Responsible Agency under CEQA in order to issue permits, in this role you will initiate, execute, and manage contracts with SCE, coordinate with consultants, and oversee the preparation of critical documents. You will guide and support the issuance of permits, ensure timely completion of environmental reviews, facilitate mitigation efforts, and assess the success of conservation measures across multiple regions.  

  

  

What You Will Do:
\- Lead a team of Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialists) in environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning for SCE projects.
\- Oversee the development and certification of CEQA documents for SCE's permits, including a Master Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (LSAA) and possibly CESA incidental take permits for projects across Regions 4, 5, and 6\.
\- Coordinate with regional and statewide staff to ensure project goals are met on time and in compliance with environmental laws and regulations.
\- Provide leadership and mentorship to your team, fostering a collaborative environment and driving success in complex, multi\-regional projects.
  

What We Are Looking For: We need someone who can take on a challenge, manage multiple complex projects, and ensure deadlines are met while maintaining the highest standards of environmental stewardship. If you are a problem\-solver with strong leadership skills and a passion for conservation, this could be the perfect role for you!  

  

  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.  

Class Title: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)/Exam Bulletin  

  

  

**This position is posted in the following counties:** *Orange/Santa Barbara/San Diego counties*. **Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.**  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The office will be located in the Seal Beach, Santa Barbara or San Diego office and must be able to travel up to 20% to attend site visits throughout the South Coast Region, including Santa Barbara, Ventura, Los Angeles, and Orange Counties. Travel outside the region up to 5% will also be required. The position involves using a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, as well as performing office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking between locations. The role includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, attending in\-person workgroups with stakeholders, and engaging with local, state, and federal agencies in the South Coast Region, as well as Regions 4 and 6\. Field site visits will be necessary, and the incumbent must be able to walk on uneven, hilly terrain. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear a uniform in accordance with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) during field surveys and public interactions, both within and outside the Region as directed by the supervisor. A valid driver's license is required travel and field site visits to remote or rural areas where alternative transportation is not feasible. Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.

**Final Filing Date:** **8/4/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you ready to take on a challenge and lead a dynamic team working on high\-profile environmental projects? The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) is seeking a Limited Term Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) to oversee the Southern California Edison (SCE) workload in our Habitat Conservation Planning Program. If you are a self\-motivated individual who thrives in fast\-paced, complex work environments and is passionate about conservation and environmental protection, we want to hear from you!  

  

  

About the Role: This is a working supervisor position where you will supervise and conduct environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning functions for SCE projects. You will play a key role in ensuring compliance with the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and Lake and Streambed Alteration (LSA) agreements, working to maintain a balance between environmental protection and project progress.  

  

  

CDFW may be serving as the Lead or Responsible Agency under CEQA in order to issue permits, in this role you will initiate, execute, and manage contracts with SCE, coordinate with consultants, and oversee the preparation of critical documents. You will guide and support the issuance of permits, ensure timely completion of environmental reviews, facilitate mitigation efforts, and assess the success of conservation measures across multiple regions.  

  

  

What You Will Do:
\- Lead a team of Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialists) in environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning for SCE projects.
\- Oversee the development and certification of CEQA documents for SCE's permits, including a Master Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (LSAA) and possibly CESA incidental take permits for projects across Regions 4, 5, and 6\.
\- Coordinate with regional and statewide staff to ensure project goals are met on time and in compliance with environmental laws and regulations.
\- Provide leadership and mentorship to your team, fostering a collaborative environment and driving success in complex, multi\-regional projects.
  

What We Are Looking For: We need someone who can take on a challenge, manage multiple complex projects, and ensure deadlines are met while maintaining the highest standards of environmental stewardship. If you are a problem\-solver with strong leadership skills and a passion for conservation, this could be the perfect role for you!  

  

  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.  

Class Title: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)/Exam Bulletin  

  

  

**This position is posted in the following counties:** *Orange/Santa Barbara/San Diego counties*. **Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.**  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The office will be located in the Seal Beach, Santa Barbara or San Diego office and must be able to travel up to 20% to attend site visits throughout the South Coast Region, including Santa Barbara, Ventura, Los Angeles, and Orange Counties. Travel outside the region up to 5% will also be required. The position involves using a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, as well as performing office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking between locations. The role includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, attending in\-person workgroups with stakeholders, and engaging with local, state, and federal agencies in the South Coast Region, as well as Regions 4 and 6\. Field site visits will be necessary, and the incumbent must be able to walk on uneven, hilly terrain. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear a uniform in accordance with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) during field surveys and public interactions, both within and outside the Region as directed by the supervisor. A valid driver's license is required travel and field site visits to remote or rural areas where alternative transportation is not feasible. Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.

jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

AECOM is actively seeking a creative, highly talented Area Manager with a focus on Environmental Site Assessment and Remediation. Area Managers are responsible for overseeing the performance of a group of major programs and/or projects to assure the achievement of internal and client\-facing KPIs. The location of this position is based in California. The successful candidate will be expected to continue to be involved in and execute billable work.

***The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:***

**Project Delivery:**

* Drives program performance to meet and/or exceed client satisfaction and KPIs.
* Understands and drives business performance and the attainment and exceedance of internal KPIs.
* Interacts with business leadership on governance \& risk issues to ensure risk management triggers are identified and addressed proactively.
* Develops and formulates solutions to client problems/issues.
* Participates in project reviews of major program/project dashboards/deep dives to identify issues and improve performance.
* Works to drive faster adoption of digital tools.
* Actively integrates international Enterprise Capabilities into project delivery to meet business targets and works with business leadership to manage transitions.
* Continually develops ideas for program and process improvement.
* Is directly engaged and manages high\-quality client projects.

**People:**

* Actively shares people management responsibilities for approximately 50 department staff.
* Builds, maintains, and facilitates trusting relationships with key contacts across the depth and breadth of three multinational chemical company client organizations.
* Serves as a focal point for major issue resolution and provides rapid follow\-up to address concerns.
* Participates in feedback for Project Managers to assure client satisfaction and long\-term growth.
* Develops and implements succession plans for the team and advises on the recruiting of key people to serve client needs.
* Assures project delivery employees are trained and mentored with a long\-term goal of training new project managers.
* Coaches project managers and team members on understanding business performance and internal KPIs; implements processes with Project Managers.
* Evaluates individual performance of project managers within the department.

**Business Development:**

* Works collaboratively with Client Account Manager(s), Practice Area Leaders, and Business Line Leadership to grow profitable backlog and ensure financial success of their respective client program.
* Develops budgets that allow for business development portfolio management, tracking \& optimizing wins and bookings, and project oversight.
* Leads capture strategies for key pursuits and major projects within the department, ensures those strategies yield high capture rates, and grows the business and relevant technical capabilities.

**Operations:**

* Acts as a point of escalation for project issues and makes recommendations to improve performance. This may include addressing project resourcing gaps, supporting technical issues, resolving invoicing and cash collection challenges, addressing subconsultant and vendor concerns, etc.
* Drives consistent project management practices and procedures in alignment with AECOM Project Delivery System (PDS) and Quality Management System (QMS) requirements.
* Ensures accuracy of Workload Planning Tool output for the department.
* Maintains departmental compliance with West Region Environment Pricing guidance and DOA approval framework.
* Ensures the accuracy of the department’s Salesforce pipeline data and associated Detailed Forecast data and output reports.

  

**Qualifications** **Minimum Requirements:**

Job Posting: Environmental Scientist

Department of Fish and Wildlife

JC-525715

Environmental Scientist

ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,418.00 - $9,321.00 per Month

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

Final Filing Date: 7/31/2026

Job Description And Duties

This person performs a variety of professional scientific office and field work primarily in the Southern Fisheries District comprised of Tulare, Kern, and Kings Counties, and assists the Inland Fisheries Unit Region-wide. Incumbent independently performs fishery resource management analysis, research, surveys, investigations, and studies; writes final reports; prepares regulatory and compliance documents; prepares non-routine correspondence and answers non-routine questions from the public. Incumbent provides consultative advice to various governmental entities and agencies. Incumbent shares responsibility for the fishery on the Kern Plateau including Little Kern Golden trout, Kern River Rainbow trout, and California Golden trout.

The South District staff lead conduct fishery studies, fish rescues, fish die-off investigations, fish population surveys (i.e. visual, e-fishing, snorkeling, and/or red surveys), exotic fish species and/or aquatic invasive species removals, water quantity/quality measurements, and site visits to evaluate site specific habitat conditions. Additionally, Incumbent provides oversight for the aquatic species on the Kern Plateau and managing any associated grants or contracts.

Personal Leave Program: Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

Link to Environmental Scientist Exam: CalCareers

This position is posted in the following counties: Fresno and Kern. Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Working Conditions

Requires Incumbent To Be Able Work In Remote Mountainous Terrain, Hike Extended Distances On Multi-day Backcountry Trips. In Order To Complete The Essential Functions Of This Position The Following Activities Are Required:

Work and drive in inclement weather.
Lift at least 45 pounds.
Work flexible hours (day and night) especially during field season, including

weekends to respond to changing weather conditions, to monitor and move

equipment, and conduct field surveys.

Use a computer several hours a day which involves sitting most of the time, but may

include walking or standing for brief periods.

Travel overnight (sometimes for multiple nights) occasionally.

Minimum Requirements

You will find the Minimum Requirements in the Class Specification.

Department Information

Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) employees are committed to managing and protecting California’s diverse wildlife and the habitats upon which they depend.

California is one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. As such, CDFW values diverse employees working together to protect nature for all Californians. CDFW is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment where all backgrounds, cultures and personal experiences can thrive and connect others to our critical mission.

Join us and begin a meaningful new career!

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
The Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for leading and managing all EHS programs within a lithium-ion battery manufacturing environment. This is a hands-on, standalone role requiring a self-motivated professional who can independently develop, implement, and maintain safety and environmental compliance programs while supporting daily manufacturing operations. The EHS Specialist will ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, and local regulatory requirements, with specific focus on chemical handling, lithium battery safety, hazardous waste management, and industrial risk prevention.

Key responsibilities

Serve as the primary EHS representative for the facility and the on-site safety resource.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve EHS policies, procedures, and training programs.
Promote a proactive safety culture across manufacturing, warehouse, and engineering teams.

Regulatory Compliance

Ensure full compliance with OSHA, EPA, state/local regulations, and industry best practices.
Maintain required EHS documentation including SDS management, incident logs, inspections, and permits.
Support regulatory audits and serve as the main contact for external agencies.

Manufacturing & Chemical Safety

Oversee safe handling and storage of lithium-ion battery materials, including electrolytes, solvents, and powders.
Implement controls for fire prevention, thermal runaway risks, and emergency response procedures.
Conduct job hazard analyses (JHAs) and risk assessments for production activities.

Compliance & audit readiness

Ensure document control practices support compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100 (if applicable), and internal ALE quality system requirements.
Support EHS-related documentation aligned with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 where applicable.
Maintain controlled records in an audit-ready state with complete approval and traceability history.
Support internal, customer, and external audits by providing controlled documents and records promptly.

Hazardous Materials & Waste Management

Manage hazardous waste programs including labeling, storage, accumulation areas, and disposal coordination.
Ensure compliance with DOT requirements for shipping lithium batteries and hazardous materials (UN 3480/3481).
Coordinate environmental reporting and waste reduction initiatives.

Training & Employee Engagement

Conduct EHS onboarding and recurring training (PPE, chemical safety, lockout/tagout, emergency response, etc.).
Lead safety meetings, toolbox talks, and incident prevention initiatives.
Provide hands-on coaching to employees on safe work practices

Incident Management & Continuous Improvement

Lead investigations for near-misses, injuries, spills, or safety events.
Track corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Monitor site safety performance metrics and recommend improvements.

Emergency Preparedness

Maintain emergency response plans including fire protection, chemical spill response, evacuation procedures, and first aid readiness.
Coordinate drills and ensure emergency equipment is inspected and functional.

Daily On-the-Floor Support

Perform routine safety inspections and audits in production and warehouse areas.
Partner closely with operations leadership to address safety concerns in real time.
Support implementation of 5S and safe manufacturing practices.

Qualification

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
3+ years of EHS experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulations and safety management systems.
Ability to work independently in a one-person EHS role and manage multiple priorities.
Experience in lithium-ion battery, chemical, electronics, or high-tech manufacturing.
Knowledge of hazardous material shipping and storage regulations (DOT/IATA).
Familiarity with ISO 14001 or ISO 45001 standards.
HAZWOPER or other relevant certifications (a plus).

Work Environment and Physical requirements

Manufacturing facility with exposure to chemicals, powered industrial equipment, and regulated battery materials.
Requires use of PPE and adherence to strict safety protocols.
May involve occasional lifting, walking production floors, and responding to urgent safety needs.
Frequent bending, squatting, reaching, and climbing.
Ability to lift up to 35 lbs.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
Ability to work safely

*Be Exceptional. Deliver Excellence. Make A Difference.*

LimnoTech is a leading environmental engineering and science firm with clients who face water\-related problems that are more challenging and costly than ever before. It is our job to help our clients make decisions based on the best available science and real\-world constraints.

Are you ready to join a team of smart, talented people who are motivated every day to deliver excellence and make a difference for our clients, our partners, and the environment?

  

LimnoTech is seeking an experienced sediment remediation specialist to lead complex environmental investigations and the design of cleanup strategies for contaminated sediment sites in riverine, lacustrine, estuarine, and marine environments. The selected candidate will be based in one of LimnoTech's primary office locations (Ann Arbor, Los Angeles, Oakdale, or DC). Come work with us!

The Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions Data Quality Assurance Section in the Program Planning and Management Branch has a vacant Air Pollution Specialist (APS) position for which it is seeking highly competent candidates with experience and expertise in natural and working lands GHG quantification and emissions reduction methods. The Section is responsible for ensuring the impartiality and quality of third\-party verifications and will oversee third\-party verifications performed as required by Senate Bill 27: Carbon sequestration: state goals: natural and working lands: registry of projects (SB 27\).  

Under direction of the Air Resources I, the APS applies scientific methods and principles in the identification, study, and solution of air pollution problems. The APS designs, conducts, and evaluates methods to reduce GHG emissions from natural and working lands. The APS specifically focuses on forests, floodplains and wetlands, coastal habitats, agriculture, and urban lands. This candidate will work in coordination with the California Natural Resources Agency to develop the Natural and Working Lands Climate Smart Strategy, as required by SB 27, and will also play a lead role in establishing carbon dioxide removal targets for 2030 and beyond, while considering the Natural and Working Lands Climate Smart Strategy, science\-based data, cost\-effectiveness, and technological feasibility in setting the targets.  

The candidate will support CARB’s efforts in developing policy through technical and policy analysis, and quantifying the costs, benefits, and equity implications of natural and working lands policies. Additionally, the candidate will identify research needs that advance CARB’s understanding of cutting\-edge issues in natural and working lands. The candidate will engage and collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, but not limited to, public agencies, research institutions, equity stakeholders, developers, industry, and other CARB staff, management, and executive leadership teams. This candidate must understand the complexities of natural and working lands and the roles that policy, technology, and the natural environment play. The candidate should also be aware of the social equity implications of natural and workin glands policies and be able to develop strategies accordingly.

jobs.title: Sr Environmental Coordinator - Air Quality
jobs.description:
Job Description

The senior environmental coordinator works with operating unit personnel to ensure awareness of and compliance with environmental permits, regulations, policies and procedures and requirements of the company, assisting the operating group in the development of solutions to environmental issues. Monitors chemical, physical and biological hazards that could be present. Investigates environmental incidents and reports incidents to appropriate regulatory agencies. Assists with the development and delivery of environmental procedures and training. Implements environmental compliance self-inspections and recommends appropriate action to facility management. Recommends improvements in processes, design, procedures and operations to minimize environmental incidents. Assists in maintaining facilities’ environmental licenses, permits and authorizations. Maintains close contact with environmental health and safety, laboratory, operations and maintenance and other company departments. Assists in maintaining facilities’ environmental licenses, permits and authorizations. Responsibilities include submittal of all environmental reports in advance of deadlines including gathering operational information necessary to track, monitor and complete reporting requirements.

Responsibilities

Monitors Imperial Valley operations to assure compliance with federal, state and local regulations. Develops and maintains an understanding of processes within business units, and assists the business unit in complying with environmental aspects through the company’s environmental management systems. Identifies, develops and implements environmental initiatives for establishing external competitive advantages.
Investigates environmental issues and incidents and recommends steps to reduce the frequency of events and to resolve compliance issues. Recommends resolutions to integrate environmental assessments of facilities into facility operations to ensure compliance with environmental requirements.
Remains current on applicable environmental laws and regulations affecting the CalEnergy operations. Performs complex environmental work requiring considerable exercise of independent analysis and judgment in environmental services. Coordinates environmental activities of consulting firms.
Provides technical assistance to CalEnergy managers and supervisors. Maintains a specialized knowledge and expertise in air issues, and utilizes such knowledge in day-to-day functions.
Seeks and obtains required permits for operating the power operations for the CalEnergy facilities. Evaluates regulatory impact and develops environmental programs and processes. Provides technical input to assist in development of project planning.
Assists in development and delivery of environmental training and follows up with observations to ensure implementation and compliance with regulatory requirements.
Assists with development and implements environmental policies and procedures for the Imperial Valley operations.
Performs administrative activities necessary for the effective coordination with other department staff, including employee safety.
Performs any additional responsibilities as requested or assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, environmental sciences, engineering, or related field and three to five years of environmental experience or equivalent work experience. (Typically six years of related, progressive work experience would be needed for candidates applying for this position who do not possess a bachelor’s degree.)
Five years of related experience.
Background working in all environmental media. Demonstrated air quality environmental industry experience is required. A broad diversity of environmental work experience in private industry, governmental, and consulting is preferred.
In-depth knowledge of applicable governmental laws and regulations. Ability to review and summarize complex regulations, with the demonstrated ability to implement environmental programs.
Effective interpersonal skills and leadership abilities. Must demonstrate the ability to coordinate projects and work with others effectively in a diverse working environment.
Excellent written and oral communications skills.
Detail oriented. Excellent organization skills. Ability to prioritize environmental responsibilities.
Intermediate to advanced knowledge of personal computer software applications, including spreadsheet, word processing and database experience.
Ability to read, analyze and interpret documents such as business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, governmental regulations. Ability to write reports, business correspondence and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, the general public and employees at all levels.
Effective analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills. Ability to calculate figures and amounts such as proportions, percentages, area, circumference and volume. Ability to apply concepts of basic algebra and geometry. Capable of drawing and interpreting graphs.
Ability to define obscure and incomplete problems collects data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions. Ability to conceptualize and develop creative alternatives to problem resolution. Ability to deal with abstract and concrete concepts.
Provides accurate input into the budget process and contributes to meeting the actual targets.
Attends work on a regular basis and supports the Company’s employee policies and procedures, including workplace safety rules.
A valid California driver’s license is required.

About Us

BHE Renewables delivers sustainable energy solutions for customers and communities. We own, operate and develop wind, solar, geothermal, hydroelectric and natural gas projects in 11 U.S. states. The power generated is sold into energy markets or directly to customers through long-term purchase agreements.
Headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa, BHE Renewables is an innovative and growing company with new offices in Phoenix and San Diego. Our 50/50 joint venture with Occidental Petroleum has led to a demonstration project showing how TerraLithium technology is used to extract lithium from the brine presently flowing through our geothermal plants in Imperial Valley, CA.
Our CHAMPION culture drives our success by fostering high expectations, ownership and continuous improvement within a respectful and inclusive team environment. Through the CHAMPION mindset, we focus on the fundamentals – preparation, planning and attention to detail – holding ourselves accountable to do simple better. We are seeking an experienced environmental scientist or engineer to join our Queensland team and play a leading role in the delivery of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.


This role is suited to an experienced consultant who enjoys technical problem solving, project leadership and working with clients to develop practical and defensible environmental solutions. The position offers exposure to a broad range of projects and sectors, including energy, resources, infrastructure, manufacturing, chemicals and heavy industry.


While a strong background in contaminated land assessment and management is important, we are particularly interested in adaptable practitioners who can apply their technical skills across a range of environmental disciplines, including compliance, approvals, environmental due diligence, environmental management and remediation.


The preferred location for this role is Brisbane; however, other Queensland locations will be considered for suitably experienced candidates. The role involves a flexible mix of office, home and field\-based work, together with periodic travel to project sites throughout Queensland and Australia.

**Typical responsibilities:**

* Lead technical delivery of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.
* Plan, coordinate and manage environmental investigations, including soil, groundwater, surface water and vapour assessment programs.
* Review, interpret and evaluate environmental data and develop technically robust and commercially practical recommendations.
* Author and review technical reports and project deliverables, including:


 o Preliminary and detailed site investigations


 o Contaminated land assessments


 o Remediation action plans and validation reports


 o Environmental management plans


 o Compliance and monitoring report


 o Environmental approvals and supporting documentation

* Provide technical leadership and quality assurance for work completed by project team members.
* Lead the technical delivery and project execution of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.
* Coordinate and supervise subcontractors and specialist service providers during field investigations and remediation works.
* Engage directly with clients, regulators, contractors and other stakeholders to support project delivery and resolve technical issues.
* Contribute to proposal preparation, scope development and cost estimation for new opportunities.
* Support the development of junior and intermediate staff through technical guidance, coaching and project leadership.
* Contribute to technical innovation and continuous improvement initiatives within the business.


As a growing business, this role provides opportunities to expand technical leadership responsibilities, strengthen client relationships, contribute to service development and play a meaningful role in the continued growth of the Queensland practice.

**Position Requirements:**


This opportunity is suited to a motivated and adaptable environmental professional who combines strong technical capability with project leadership and client management skills. The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* Strong technical knowledge of contaminated land assessment, remediation and environmental management principles.
* Excellent analytical and critical\-thinking skills, with the ability to develop practical and defensible solutions to complex environmental challenges.
* Exceptional written communication skills and demonstrated experience preparing high\-quality technical reports and client deliverables.
* Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Proven ability to manage projects, coordinate multidisciplinary teams and deliver successful outcomes.

* Strong understanding of the ASC NEPM and Queensland contaminated land regulatory framework.
* Experience managing environmental field programs, including soil, groundwater and surface water investigations.
* Demonstrated experience leading the preparation and review of high\-quality technical reports and client deliverables.

* Experience working across multiple environmental service areas such as compliance, approvals, environmental management, due diligence or remediation would be highly regarded.

Department of Pesticide Regulation


JC-525317Environmental Scientist


ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST
$4,418.00 - $9,321.00 per Month


New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


Final Filing Date: 8/19/2026


Job Description and Duties
Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you! The Department of Pesticide Regulation's (DPR) Enforcement Regional Office Branch is recruiting one Environmental Scientist in the Southern Regional Office (SRO) located in the city of Santa Ana.




Under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisor), the incumbent will perform professional scientific analyses and fieldwork associated with appropriate use of pesticides; independently apply scientific methods and principles to identify, research, analyze, and develop science-based solutions for compliance with complex regulatory pesticide issues; provide oversight of enforcement activities to maintain statewide uniformity; generate, analyze and evaluate scientific data for regulatory compliance with human health and environmental requirements to ensure protection of human health, non-target organisms, food safety, surface/ground water, wildlife, and air quality.


You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement.




Working Conditions
The collection of samples as indicated for this position requires the ability to lift and carry a minimum of 25 pounds, bend, squat, and climb over boxes, containers, or pallets; travel by automobile or air may be required to different areas of the State.
